question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit Slack outbound recipient allowlist now, and should it be Slack-specific config or part of a shared human-chat outbound target policy?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the fix adds a public authorization config under a documented trusted-operator security model, so automation should not choose the product/security boundary.

options.title: Add shared outbound target policy
options.body: Define an allowTo-style outbound recipient policy with shared send-boundary enforcement and Slack schema/docs/tests as the first implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader guardrails
options.body: Track Slack recipient allowlisting as one acceptance case under #87870 so sanitizer, verified delivery, and target authorization are designed together.

options.title: Decline core allowTo for now
options.body: Keep the trusted-operator model unchanged and document that dmPolicy and allowFrom do not constrain explicit operator sends.

recommendation.title: Add shared outbound target policy
recommendation.body: Define an allowTo-style outbound recipient policy with shared send-boundary enforcement and Slack schema/docs/tests as the first implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: The issue combines Slack DM policy, explicit message sends, and trusted-operator security framing where steipete has the strongest history signal.
